get_user_tenant_id() resolves impersonation from the JWT, not just the user row

Anon/public read surface for the booking site (faqs, testimonials, promotions, cms_pages, cms_media, vehicle_photos)
Double-entry financial core: ledger_entries charges vs payments, reconciled by remaining_amount
pnl_entries as the Profit & Loss reporting feed (income/expense side + source_ref)

Expense Tracker: business-expense ledger built by widening vehicle_expenses
Design: vehicle_id NULL means a business/overhead expense, not a vehicle cost
Decision: expense category is free text (enum retired), only loosely coupled to expense_categories rows
handle_vehicle_expense_pnl trigger keeps P&L in lockstep via the vexp:{id} reference key
H1: replacing or removing a receipt orphans the old file in the paid private bucket
H2: expense-receipts bucket policies authorize on bucket_id alone — cross-tenant read/delete of financial documents
Fix: scope storage policies to storage.foldername(name)[1] = get_user_tenant_id()
Receipts live in a private bucket served by 10-minute signed URLs, never public links
M1: changing a category's P&L bucket never reflows historical pnl_entries — config and P&L silently disagree
M2: deleting a category orphans its expenses and there is no rename — the edit dialog then fails validation
M3: is_recurring can save true with a null recurrence_interval (the select only displays the default)
M4: two divergent write paths into vehicle_expenses — the legacy vehicle dialog still hardcodes the retired category enum
Codebase-wide convention: RLS enforces tenant scope only; role/permission gating lives in the app, so a viewer-manager can still write via the API
L1: no pagination — the whole tenant's expense set is loaded, then searched and reduced in memory
CSV export deliberately exports only the filtered in-memory view — a pagination change would silently truncate it
Roadmap: make the recurring toggle real via a cron job reusing the PAYG / auto-extension cron pattern
Roadmap: reuse the existing ai-document-ocr function to autofill vendor/amount/date from a receipt
Resolution: H1/H2, M1-M4 and L1-L8 shipped with two migrations; M5 deliberately left as-is to match the codebase norm
Pre-build edge-case audit of the cron simulation design — 24 gaps, binding amendments before any code
Blocker 1: sim_shift RPC is an open door — EXECUTE never revoked from PUBLIC, no column allowlist, no env guard, unbounded p_days
Blocker 2: identity checks must key on app_users.auth_user_id, not app_users.id — this repo was bitten by the same mistake before
Blocker 3: the v1 golden path does nothing — the fixture rental is created as Pending with NULL PAYG columns while the job filters status='Active', and every failure green-toasts
Blocker 4: a freshly wiped staging project has no super-admin login identity at all — admin-create-user only yields head_admin and emergency-bootstrap hardcodes prod
Blocker 5: rotating the JWT secret kills the anon key that every app hardcodes as a client fallback — the planned Phase-0 rotation is a production outage
Major 6: manual dispatch overlapping cron double-charges — process-installment-payment creates PaymentIntents with no idempotency key or lock
Major 7: force_test_mode and NOTIFICATIONS_DISABLED are read by zero lines — safety must assert the absence of the keys that actually send
Major 8: functions.invoke swallows non-2xx bodies, so 403/401/412 are indistinguishable and a catch-up-capped run looks broken
Major 9: time travel must shift payg_next_accrual_at, payg_start_ts and start_date as one coherent unit or accruals predate the rental
Major 10: one-way transitions (auto_extend_paused, plan overdue, collection_mode='manual') can kill a fixture in one click — mark them irreversible in the manifest
Major 11: anti-rot triple gap — staleness stamped at sync not deploy, never displayed, and the drift-checker has no trigger
Major 12: some columns are disqualifying when backdated — payments.created_at anchors recover-pending-stripe-payments to real now, so shift() must refuse it
Major 13 / prod bug: daily-reminders buckets are exact midnight-UTC floor math, so the 'due today' bucket is unreachable after 00:00 UTC
Major 14: shared staging — a global fire sweeps another dev's fixtures and wipe/sync are global nukes; scope with an advisory lock and cleanupTenant()
Prod bug: the installment plan SELECT omits failure_count so handleFailure always writes 1 — the >=3 overdue cascade is unreachable in production
Prod bug: the payment_intent.canceled webhook handler cancels rentals with no status guard
Amendment A7: per-job advisory-lock lease (409 when held) plus a scenario-scope lock, so dispatch can never overlap cron
Minor 24: catch-up is tenant-aware maxDaysFor(), so scenarios must assert final DB state and never dispatch counts
Minor 17: Stripe Sandbox delivers delayed events for up to 7 real days, so fixtures are same-day disposable and teardown must cancel its own PIs
Binding amendments A1-A8 / B1-B6 that the DevPanel and simulation designs must absorb before build
A deposit hold is a card authorization, not a deposit — funds are ringfenced by the issuer and the DB row is only our claim
Hard ceiling: no card network permits an authorization beyond 30 days (Visa 29d18h; Visa Table 5-12 caps vehicle rental at 30)
'90 days' means N consecutive cancel-and-recreate cycles — the reliability of the cycle, not the duration of one hold, is the engineering problem
Compliance unknown that can void the whole duration workstream: extended validity is documented for unknown final amounts, and a fixed damage buffer may not qualify
Bug 1 (critical): every throw in the refresh loop writes terminal deposit_hold_status='expired', and the driver query only selects 'held' — one transient error destroys the deposit forever, silently
Bug 2 (critical): refresh cancels the live PaymentIntent before the replacement exists, so any failure between the two leaves no hold at all
Bug 3 (critical): the tenants lookup and getConnectAccountId throw before Stripe is ever called, so one transient read failure marks every held deposit for that tenant expired in a single pass
Bug 4: place-deposit-hold hand-rolls a two-rung fallback and never tries the extended-auth-only rung, silently forfeiting ~30-day holds if only multicapture is refused
Bug 5: the refresh idempotency key is derived from the old PaymentIntent id, which the failure path never updates — so any retry within 24h replays Stripe's cached decline verbatim
Rationale: the idempotency-replay bug is invisible in staging because a fresh fixture per run always mints a new key — it needs a unit test, not a sandbox run
Bug 6: deduct-from-deposit does a bare partial capture and forces status 'captured' — Stripe auto-releases the remainder, so deducting $200 of $1,500 silently frees $1,300

Bug 7: Checkout-placed holds are recorded only by the success_url redirect — metadata.type='security_deposit_hold' has no webhook handler, so closing the tab strands the renter's money with no DB record
Bug 8: refresh anchors the platform to rentals.platform_account but reads currency from the tenant's current row — a UK to UAE migration mid-rental guarantees a failed replacement hold
Bug 9: payment_intent.canceled sets rentals.status='Cancelled' guarded only by 'a payments row exists' — an authorization aging out can cancel a live Active rental
Bug 10 / W10: refresh-deposit-holds runs with verify_jwt=false and honours a caller-supplied only_rental_id — anyone with a rental UUID can force a destructive re-auth cycle
Bug 11: sync-deposit-hold rewrites rentals.platform_account unconditionally from the tenant's current model, so a browser redirect can re-anchor a UK rental to UAE
Bug 12: refresh reuses rentals.deposit_hold_payment_method_id verbatim and nothing updates it when a customer changes card — guaranteed eventual failure on a long rental
Bug 13: when capture_before is simply absent, resolveHoldExpiry falls through to a silent +7d fallback, so the DB row can outlive the real authorization
Bug 14: rows invisible to the cron forever — .lt() against a NULL deposit_hold_expires_at yields NULL, and Pending rentals are excluded although three writers set 'held' with no status guard
Bug 15: every loop write is unguarded and discards its { error } (supabase-js resolves rather than throws), stranding rentals in 'refreshing' with a live untracked PaymentIntent
Bug 16: the refresh loop is serial and unbounded while edge functions die at 150s idle / 400s wall clock — a mid-loop kill strands rentals nothing reaps
Bug 17: the auto_extend_enabled release branch evaluates after the unconditional cancel, so 'release instead of refresh' actually means 'destroy, then record that we released'
Bug 18: the card-feature fallback ladder triggers on a substring match of an English Stripe error string — a reword would expire every hold on every ineligible account in one nightly pass
Bug 21: two different things are both called a 'deposit hold' — booking pre-auths carry a payments row, rental deposit holds do not, so any merged reporting double-counts
Bug 22: none of the deposit logic has ever been asserted — the portal test tree contains no 'deposit' anywhere, so every proposed design assumed a test layer that does not exist
Rollout rule: every behavioural change lands behind a DEPOSIT_V2_TENANTS allowlist, and place/refresh are never deployed in the same release so a dead deposit can be attributed
W1: route deposit failures through notifyOperatorsInApp with a dedupeKey, on the existing payment_failed type so bell plus email arrive with zero DDL
Rationale: run the reconciliation backfill before enabling alerting, or day one is an alert storm, the channel gets muted and the alerting is worthless
Do not build alerting on reminders-generate / reminders-digest: the digest's send step is a TODO plus a console.log and the generator's only caller is an uncalled hook
Verified fact: refresh-deposit-holds is pg_cron jobid 57 at 0 3 * * *, active with 56 succeeded runs — but 'succeeded' only means pg_net dispatched the request
W2: decline triage — transient / funds / SCA / dead-card classes each map to a next state and backoff, capped at 8 attempts because issuers read more as fraud

Explicit decision: do NOT reorder to create-before-cancel — two simultaneous full-amount authorizations can themselves cause the insufficient_funds decline they were meant to prevent, and worsen debit stacking
W3: create-connected-account never sets business_profile.mcc, so Stripe auto-assigned one — MCC gates Amex/Discover extended auth entirely and a 0.08% surcharge
W3: persist extended_authorization.status and the true capture_before, otherwise the DB can never answer whether a hold got 30 days or 7
W4: a charge-saved-card edge function — off-session confirm on the record-anchored platform, payments row with booking_source 'admin', operator reason and audit row
Mislabel: the portal's 'Charge via Stripe' button does not charge — it opens a Checkout URL and should be renamed 'Send payment link'
W5: a rental_card_mandates row written from the signed agreement — Visa's Stored Credential Framework requires disclosing frequency and amount determination and keeping the record
The agreement template describes a single static hold released at return, not a cancel-and-replace series run 3-18 times — this gap, not duration, is the real deception exposure
CA Civ. Code 1939.15 and NY GBL 396-z(7) are scoped to rentals under 30 days — so papering a 90-day rental as chained short extensions drags every segment back inside NY's outright ban
W7: tenants.deposit_policy tiering — hold / on_file / charge_refund — because a 90-day and a 3-day rental are not the same product
Invariant: rentals.deposit_hold_payment_method_id is also the auto-extend rent-charging card — deleting the 'pointless probe hold' silently kills auto-extend auto-charge
charge_refund has no ledger representation: migration 20260420120500 deliberately removed the Security Deposit charge, so a real deposit would land as an unallocated payment
W6: a reconcile-deposit-holds poller that forces the DB to match Stripe for every non-terminal deposit state, including cancelling orphaned prior PaymentIntents
Rationale: a poller not a charge.expired webhook — the holds are direct charges on the connected account, so events only arrive if the endpoint was registered with connect:true (unverified)
Visa's Misuse of Authorization System Fee is assessed on authorizations matched to neither a clearing transaction nor a reversal — at 13-18 pairs per rental any systematic miss multiplies
Sharpest customer-harm risk: debit holds can take weeks to clear, so a re-auth cadence lets a renter carry several ringfenced deposits while Stripe shows exactly one
Card expiry mid-rental is likely on 90 days and completely unmonitored — no payment_method.automatically_updated handler, and brand change is a hard stop for merchant-initiated charges
authentication_required has no server-side fix — it needs a dedicated action_required state and an on-session re-place link, which also converts the transaction to customer-initiated
Testing gap: the sandbox seeds its fixture on the platform test account and all test tenants share one Connect account, so the card-feature ineligibility branch cannot be reproduced at all
sandbox-refresh-deposit-holds is a hand-maintained verbatim fork — every change must be mirrored or staging stops modelling production
Widening the refresh driver query widens the Time Machine's preview, so assertBlastRadius must be re-run before and after every query change or the harness goes dark
W9: the rental page branches on held / expired / falsy only, so refreshing, processing and failed render no deposit action at all, and deposit_hold_expires_at is shown nowhere
W9: the customer 'Update Card' flow is hidden behind having an installment plan, so a long-term renter cannot change their card and staff cannot do it for them
The Stripe ticket: 12 written questions, led by whether extended authorization is even a permitted use for a fixed-amount deposit — a 'no' voids the rest
Open decisions that block workstreams: reserved funds vs ability to collect, GMT's operating state, one agreement vs chained extensions, and whether a deliberate double-hold is acceptable
Cross-domain seam critique of the chained-hold designs: every finding lives between two domains that each read only half the code
The unjoined file: flipPaymentModel nulls stripe_customer_id for EVERY customer of the tenant, justified in-code by a readiness gate whose premise is false three times over
S1: after the UAE flip the chain survives but every recovery action dies — no hold can be re-placed, and a card update mints a UAE payment method onto a UK-anchored chain
resource_missing reaching release-deposit-hold is swallowed as success and written as terminal 'released' — funds stay authorized while the DB says released
The migration readiness gate filters only held/processing, so it cannot see refreshing or failed — precisely the states a crashed link leaves behind — and the admin button is labelled 'Flip anyway'
S2: 0 3 * * * UTC is 21:00-22:00 Central for GMT, and GMT is a self-service lockbox operator whose late key drops and returns are the design intent
S2 net effect: key handover releases while the cron is mid-refresh, the cron then overwrites with a fresh full-amount hold on a Closed rental that no query will ever look at again
S3: an SCA-expired hold plus the -recollect-{status} idempotency suffix replays the cached requires_action response, producing a wrong 'card declined' message and a 24h lockout

S4: both capture paths are broken differently — deduct-from-deposit is category-locked and gated on a ledger charge that no longer exists, and full capture books a phantom Security Deposit charge FIFO excludes
S5: place-deposit-hold blocks on any rental_extensions row with no status filter, so an extended rental runs with no authorization on a contract that promised one
S6: the deposit-hold customer/PM columns are auto-extend's only card-on-file source, and three separate proposals would rewrite or null them — record it as an explicit invariant first
S7: a reconciler that backfills payments rows for hold PaymentIntents arms the payment_intent.canceled rental-cancel landmine on every rental it touches
S8: running the current unguarded loop four times more often quadruples the release/refresh race — the schedule change is only safe after optimistic concurrency lands
S9 / Gate -1: extract the per-rental refresh body into _shared so cron and sandbox import one copy — otherwise every fix lands twice and the harness green-lights code production no longer runs
C3: never chain a hold on a Pending rental — re-authorizing a card every few days for a car nobody collected is indefensible; release aged Pending holds and force-replace at handover
C4: renaming metadata.type before the webhook guard ships silently re-arms the rental-cancel landmine — the guard must also match by PaymentIntent id
C5: payment_apply_fifo_v2 is category-blind, so routing a hold capture through plain FIFO would silently pay a Damage charge — captures need an explicit non-damage allowlist
V1: Visa 5.7.2.4 and 5.8.8.4 both exclude potential damage, theft and other delayed charges — so speculative fuel, mileage overage and late-return exposure may not sit in the authorized amount at all
V2: create-before-cancel authorizes 2x the estimate systematically, 13-18 times per rental — defensible only with explicit overlap disclosure, seconds-long overlap and never on debit
V4: deduct-from-deposit labels operator-initiated deductions with Stripe reason 'requested_by_customer' — a bad fact in every dispute file
Strict gate ordering: violating any arrow makes the chain less safe than doing nothing
Gate 0: disarm before amplifying — payment_intent.canceled must ignore deposit-hold PIs, and checkout.session.completed must route the hold metadata without minting a payments row
Gate 1: record-anchor the connect account, mode and currency at placement; resource_missing must never write a terminal state; move the payment-model flip server-side
Gate 2: optimistic concurrency on every deposit write, a non-terminal refresh_failed with attempt counter, monotonic idempotency keys, and a stale-refreshing sweeper
Gate 3: captures route to real charges through a non-damage category allowlist, partial capture re-enabled and bounded, deduct merged into capture, expiry fallback dropped to 4 days
Gate 4: the hold is placed from booking-success before any agreement exists, so the checkout copy — not the agreement — must carry the estimate and repeat-authorization notice
Escalation: GMT cannot migrate to UAE while chained holds are live — a PaymentIntent, Customer and PaymentMethod cannot move between platform accounts, so the readiness gate may never go green
Nothing in the codebase reads card.funding, so debit-specific policy cannot be enforced anywhere today
Escalation: no policy exists anywhere for a vehicle on the road when the chain dies unrecoverably — recall, fee, or accept the unsecured days
The auto-extend release branch exists because renewal pricing replaces a damage buffer — true then, false for an anticipated-charges hold, and reversing it re-litigates a prior incident
Escalation: Visa's delayed-charge workflow (documentation, quote, alternative estimate, 20-business-day wait) is 0% implemented, so removing damage from the hold leaves an unpriced insurance decision
